head: pr17399-r3
report:
I found four defects the author should fix before merge, plus one lower-priority robustness issue. I checked these by reading the code. I did not write or run a probe for any of them, so the triggers below are untested. The only thing I ran was the existing `rename.test.ts` and `title-generator.test.ts` suites (96 pass, 0 fail), which exercise the "extra tick" concern noted in the title-generator comment.

## 1. Codex websocket reconnect can close another caller's socket while it is still connecting
**Mechanism:** `getOrCreateCodexWebSocketConnection` (diff lines 1971–2043) now loops. After `holdBeforeDispatch(hold, signal)` it does `if (round < 2 && (current?.isOpen() || current?.isConnecting())) continue;`. From the third round on, that check no longer applies, so the code runs `state.connection?.close("reconnect")` on whatever socket is current, even one another caller has just opened or is still connecting.

The comment kept just above this loop says why that is wrong: closing a CONNECTING socket fails the concurrent caller with "websocket closed before open", which turns websockets off for the whole session. The patch moved the hold into the connect path and reintroduced exactly that teardown.

**Trigger (untested):**
1. Use an `openai-codex-responses` model with websockets preferred.
2. Hold a request on `/pause`, or use any `beforeDispatch` that waits.
3. While it is held, have other callers (prewarm, a side turn, compaction V2) start a new handshake each time this caller passes the hold.
4. After two `continue`s, the third round closes the other caller's socket.

The window is narrow, but the failure persists for the session.

**Fix:** after the round limit, join or reuse the current socket (or fail this caller) instead of closing it.

## 2. `wrapTransport` / live-build machinery is new public API with no production caller
**Mechanism:** The patch adds:
- `StreamOptions.wrapTransport` and the `TransportWrapper` type.
- The stamp fields `live`, `wraps` and `unheld`.
- `layerWrapper`, plus a branch that pushes new holds onto a live build's shared `holds` array in place.

A grep of `packages/` with tests excluded finds `wrapTransport` only in `ai/src/types.ts` and `ai/src/utils/transport-fetch.ts`. Nothing outside tests passes it.

The in-place `stamp.holds.push(addHold)` path is the risky part: if anyone ever reuses a live build, holds from earlier requests stay attached and gate later ones. The documentation only forbids that ("never share it between requests"). This adds complexity to the transport every request uses, for a feature nothing in this PR needs.

**Fix:** remove `wrapTransport` and the live/layering branches from this PR, or land them with their caller.

## 3. Every request with `beforeDispatch` now dispatches asynchronously, contradicting the "costs no microtask" claim
**Mechanism:** Before the patch, `withProviderInFlightLimit` returned `healLeakedThinking(model, dispatch(false))` synchronously when no in-flight limit was set. Now any `hold` sends the request through the async outer stream, and `await holdBeforeDispatch(...)` runs even when the gate is open.

On top of that, `buildTransportFetch`'s inner fetch always awaits `holdAllBeforeDispatch(holds, signal)` before `base(...)`. The agent loop now always passes a `beforeDispatch` closure, so every turn pays this:
- an extra stream layer,
- an async IIFE,
- two hold invocations (chokepoint plus transport), both of which call `waitForProcessPause` and fire `onPauseChange` while paused.

`AgentPauseGate.dispatchHold`'s doc comment ("an open gate costs a request no microtask") and the title-generator comment both say this cost is avoided; for the provider dispatch itself it is not. The existing rename/title tests still pass, so I have no failing case — this is a contract and perf mismatch, not a demonstrated break.

**Fix:** add a synchronous fast path in `withProviderInFlightLimit` and `holdAllBeforeDispatch`: when `limit === undefined`, call `hold()` and dispatch synchronously if it returns `undefined`. The pause hold returns `undefined` when the gate is open.

## 4. GitLab Duo is now subject to the provider in-flight limit, despite the comment
**Mechanism:** `streamSimpleRequest` for `gitlab-duo-agent` now wraps in `withProviderInFlightLimit(model, opts, ...)` (diff lines 2581–2585). That calls `resolveProviderInFlightLimit(model.provider, options)` and, if a limit applies, acquires a cross-process lease. Before the patch, GitLab Duo never took a slot.

The new comment says "the wrapper heals the same way, so nothing else changes here". That is false whenever `maxInFlightRequests` or a provider concurrency setting applies. Duo workflows are long-lived sockets, so taking a slot can starve other requests.

**Trigger (untested):** set `maxInFlightRequests: 1` (or a provider `maxConcurrency`) for a gitlab-duo model and run two requests at once. The second now waits.

**Fix:** pass the hold without the limit, or document the change and add it to the CHANGELOG.

## 5. Callers that wait on the pause before their own `try` now throw on abort instead of returning their "no result" value
**Mechanism:** Several call sites added `await agentPauseGate.dispatchHold(signal)()` outside their existing error handling. `dispatchHold` rejects with `signal.reason` when the wait is aborted (`signal?.throwIfAborted()` after `waitUntilResumed`).

For example, in `generateTextReviewContextSummary`, an abort before the patch reached `completeSimple`, which returned `stopReason: "aborted"`, and the function returned `undefined`. Now an abort while paused throws out of the function. `image-gen`, `speech-enhancer` and `OmpCommitInference` follow the same pattern.

**Trigger (untested):** `/pause`, start an annotate review (or a TTS rewrite), then cancel it. The caller gets a rejection instead of `undefined`/`null`.

**Fix:** catch the abort at those call sites, or check `signal.aborted` after `waitUntilResumed` and return the existing fallback.

## 6. (Lower) The transport stops the response timer and never restarts it when a hold throws something other than an abort
**Mechanism:** `buildTransportFetch`'s inner fetch calls `deadline?.suspend()` first and calls `deadline?.resume()` only on the success path.

If `holdAllBeforeDispatch` throws a non-abort error, the guard stays suspended: its timer is cleared and its held-work window stays open until the provider calls `clear()`. Such errors include:
- `codexPrewarmHold`,
- `assertEphemeralTurnReady`,
- the sharpshooter "Session disposed" hold,
- the `MAX_DISPATCH_HOLD_PASSES` `ProviderResponseError`.

**Risk (untested):** a provider that retries on the same guarded signal after such an error, or one that does not clear the guard in `finally`, keeps reporting local work and runs without a response timeout.

**Fix:** wrap the hold in `try/catch` and call `resume()` (or `clear()`) on any throw.
